chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-R ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever drinks wine (khamr) after God forbade it through my tongue, is not worthy of being married when he proposes, nor is his intercession accepted when he intercedes, nor is he believed when he speaks, nor is he trusted with a trust. And whoever trusts him after knowing about him, there is no guarantee for the one who trusted him with God, nor is there reward for him, nor is there a substitute for him.'

key_terms.يُزَوَّجَ: To be married / eligibility for marriage
key_terms.يُشَفَّعَ: To be interceded for / acceptance of intercession

ai.seo_question: What are the legal and social consequences for a person who drinks wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration linking the consumption of *khamr* to a comprehensive erosion of social trustworthiness (*amanah*) and legal efficacy. The hadith specifies that the offender loses eligibility for marriage proposals, acceptance of intercession (*shafa'ah*), credibility in speech (*sidq*), and reliability in financial deposits, with the trustor bearing the risk if they proceed despite knowing the defect. This reflects the Shia juristic view that habitual intoxication constitutes a major moral and legal defect (*'urfan*) affecting one's standing in community affairs.
